senses.gloss:
veśá, m.
 —1. settler; neighbor.
 —2. (settlement,
 i. e.) dwelling, house. [√viś: cf.
οἶκος, ‘house,’ Old Lat. veicus, Lat. vīcus,
‘houses, quarter of a town, village’: hence
the borrowed AS. wīc, ‘town,’ as in Eoforwīc,
Eng. York, prop. ‘Eber-stadt’ or
‘Boar-town,’ and perhaps in Nor-wich,
‘Nor-ton.’]

véśman, n. (settlement, i. e.) dwelling,
house, abode, chamber. [√viś, 1168. 1a.]
